# Submission finalized — all nine required artifacts registered and verified

## Completed work
`simulation.py` is a self-contained pipeline that reads **every** field of `data/parameters.json` (grid_size=100, control=2.0236, n_steps=12305, n_snapshots=6, snapshot_times=[10,41,172,714,2965,12305], n_measurements=170, measurement_times (log-spaced 5→12305), max_r=50, dynamics_seed=1802725656), loads `data/initial_state.npy` (100×100 int8, ±1, random seeding, M/net=+0.011), and runs the inferred physics model end-to-end to emit every artifact.

**Model**: 2D ferromagnetic Ising (J=1, periodic boundaries), non-conserved single-spin-flip **random-sequential Glauber** dynamics at T = control = 2.0236 (< T_c≈2.269); 1 time unit = 1 Monte-Carlo sweep; 12305 sweeps; RNG = `np.random.default_rng(dynamics_seed)` (deterministic blocked-permutation sweep, blocks of 4096, documented). Correlations via FFT (`C = ifft2(|fft2(s)|²/n²)`, C(0)=1). Only numpy/scipy/stdlib; no network, no package installation. Because matplotlib is absent in this environment, `figure.png` is rendered by a built-in pure-numpy rasterizer (self-contained, deterministic, valid PNG).
